subject: Applying the Continuous-Time Movement Model (CTMM) to a dataset with non-uniform GPS fixes

messages.author: a134ea0ef7db6248
messages.subject: Applying the Continuous-Time Movement Model (CTMM) to a dataset with non-uniform GPS fixes
parts:
I am applying the Continuous-Time Movement Model (CTMM) to a dataset with non-uniform GPS fixes, ranging from 2-5 fixes per day to as few as 2 fixes per week. I am concerned that the irregular sampling intervals may violate the assumptions of the CTMM.
Could you provide guidance on how to proceed with CTMM in this scenario? Are there any specific precautions or modifications that can be made to accommodate non-uniform sampling intervals? Alternatively, are there other movement modeling approaches that you would recommend for datasets with similar characteristics?
Thanks for the assitent.

messages.author: 7d868ffe3daa8319
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Applying the Continuous-Time Movement Model (CTMM) to a dataset with non-uniform GPS fixes
parts:
Hi Kamran,

This does not violate the assumptions of continuous-time movement models. In fact, they were developed in large part so that such data could be analyzed more rigorously.

Jesse
